ggexon

Genomic visualization across scales

Grammar of genomic annotations, synteny, and associated data.

ggexon extends ggplot2 to combine gene models, DNA alignments, RNA-seq coverage, and protein variation in one figure. Prepare the data and layout in a Syn object, then add the layers you want to inspect.

A SynIndividual stores one genome or sample and its annotation layers. A SynSpecies groups individuals with their alignments, homology mappings, and panel layouts. Syn-aware plotting layers retrieve stored data for the selected individuals and genomic windows. Scales control coordinate transformations; themes control appearance.

Installation

ggexon is a development package. Install it from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("DongyaoLiu/ggexon")

If your R installation cannot resolve the Bioconductor dependencies, install them first:

install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c(
  "Biostrings", "GenomeInfoDb", "GenomicRanges", "Rsamtools", "rtracklayer"
))

BigWig-backed examples run on macOS and Linux. ODGI-backed graph alignment workflows also require Python 3.8 or newer and odgi.

From a Syn object to a plot

Start with the bundled HLA-A reference annotation. Construct and inspect an individual, add it to a comparison, then draw its exon-intron model:

library(ggexon)
library(ggplot2)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", "hla_a_lollipop", package = "ggexon")
reference <- SynIndividual(
  id = "HLA-A",
  annotation_file = file.path(demo_dir, "hla_a_reference.gff3"),
  annotation_format = "gff"
)
reference <- load_annotation(reference)
exons <- query_features(reference, feature_type = "exon", all = TRUE)

comparison <- SynSpecies(name = "HLA-A reference") |>
  add_individual(reference)

ggexon(comparison) +
  geom_exon2(compress_introns = FALSE) +
  facet_genomics(vars(track)) +
  scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 3) +
  theme_ggexon_track()

This example uses allele-local HLA-A coordinates. Exon widths retain their native scale, and the shared x scale shortens introns three-fold. The GFF3 is enough for annotation plotting; supply genome_file for sequence extraction or translation.

For comparative figures, attach alignments and signals to the same object, then store panel windows before plotting. Preparation verbs such as prepare_genomic_layout() and prepare_gene_lollipop() store derived views for reuse. Inspect them with their query_*() counterparts before drawing.

The four tutorials below use bundled data and follow the same sequence: prepare the Syn object, inspect its contents, and build the plot layer by layer.

1. Projecting amino acid changes onto transcript models

Project 1,212 amino-acid substitutions from 5,998 eligible named HLA-A alleles onto the reference protein and its exon-intron model. The tutorial prepares protein annotations, projects them through the reference CDS, and stores a shared genomic layout before plotting. Lollipop heights describe database allele counts, not population frequencies.

Explore the HLA-A protein and gene-model tutorial.

2. Comparing alternatively spliced transcripts

Compare human and chimpanzee AS3MT transcripts with a paper-defined human exon-skipping reconstruction. Build the comparative object first, then add transcript models, nucleotide ribbons, and aligned DNA at the exon-1 repeat. One shared x scale compresses introns while preserving exon widths and the alignment between layers.

Explore the AS3MT transcript and DNA tutorial.

3. Visualizing local synteny across species

Combine conserved flanking genes, a reconstructed three-exon Dox model in D. simulans, nucleotide alignments, and testis RNA-seq across three Drosophila species. Prepare annotations, alignments, and combined RNA-seq tracks in one object, then build the figure layer by layer. Each assembly retains its genomic axis. RNA panels share one y range and preserve their signal values; the tutorial identifies the deposited signals and remapped read depths by their source units.

Explore the three-species Dox synteny tutorial.

4. Visualizing megabase-scale haplotypes

Compare Siamang H1, Gorilla H1, and Human CHM13 across 3.63 Mb MHC windows. prepare_gene_lollipop() assigns the 58 selected MHC genes to a shared four-row, six-column grid and stores their native anchors in the Syn object. geom_gene_lollipop() retrieves that preparation automatically. Matching gene keys occupy the same cells, with empty cells reserved. Small native gene arrows, grey background genes, and direct DNA-alignment ribbons retain the genomic context below the enlarged heads.

Explore the MHC haplotype tutorial.

Package map

The main containers and preparation functions are:

Task Objects or functions
Store genomes and annotations SynIndividual, SynFeatureAnnotation, SynBigWigAnnotation, SynVCFAnnotation
Store protein features SynProteinDomainAnnotation, SynProteinMutationAnnotation
Build comparisons SynSpecies, SynPairAlignment, SynMultiAlignment, HomologyAnnotation
Attach evidence add_individual(), add_annotation(), add_pairwise_alignment(), add_homology_annotation()
Inspect stored data query_features(), query_signal(), query_variants(), query_domains()
Prepare reusable views project_mutations_to_genome(), prepare_genomic_layout(), prepare_gene_lollipop()
Prepare panel layouts store_chain_layout(), set_panel_xlim(), SynLayout, SynLocusSet
Draw models and evidence geom_exon2(), geom_genetag(), geom_gene_lollipop(), geom_nuclink(), geom_coverage(), geom_protein_lollipop()
Set scales and appearance facet_genomics(), scale_x_ggexon_genomic(), theme_ggexon_track(), theme_ggexon_clean()

Use the function reference for supported inputs, selectors, and additional geoms. Ordinary ggplot2 layers, scales, themes, and ggsave() remain available.

Learn more

Start with 0. Basic usage for data objects, geoms, scales, and panel layouts. Browse the tutorials for the four complete examples, or use the function reference for individual classes and verbs.

The archived HOX matrix example retains the gene-slot comparison, plotting code, and source audit trail.

Citation

ggexon was developed while visualizing the sept-1/zina-1 toxin-antidote locus. If you use the package in your work, please also cite:

Liu D, Zheng C. sept-1/zina-1 is an Ancient Toxin-Antidote System in Caenorhabditis elegans. bioRxiv. 2025. https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.11.28.691152v1
